title: Sternocleidomastoid
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 11.2 Naming Skeletal Muscles; 11.3 Axial Muscles of the Head, Neck, and Back; 13.4

main.t: The neck muscle from the sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process that turns and tilts the head.

simpler.t: It is the long muscle on each side of your neck that turns your head.

deeper.t: Acting alone it turns the head to the opposite side; both together flex the head.

facts.t: It runs up the side of the neck, from the sternum and clavicle to the skull behind the ear.
It inserts on the mastoid process of the temporal bone and on the occipital bone.

simpler.t: You can feel it on the side of your neck when you turn your head.

deeper.t: Seen from the side, it divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.

items.name: Sternal head
items.t: Arises from the sternum (“sterno” in the name).

items.name: Clavicular head
items.t: Arises from the clavicle (“cleido” in the name).

items.name: Insertion
items.t: On the mastoid process of the temporal bone (“mastoid” in the name), and the occipital bone.

items.name: Name
items.t: Named for its attachments, with the origin first: sterno, cleido, mastoid.

simpler.t: Its long name lists where it starts and ends: breastbone, collarbone, mastoid.

deeper.t: When a muscle is named for its attachments, the origin is always named first.

facts.t: One muscle alone turns the head to the opposite side and tilts it to its own side.
Both together flex the head forwards.

simpler.t: One side turns your head; both sides bend it forwards.

items.name: Splenius capitis
items.t: Tilts and turns the head to its own side; both together extend the head.

items.name: Semispinalis capitis
items.t: Extends the head when both sides act, opposing the sternocleidomastoids.

items.name: Accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI)
items.t: A purely motor cranial nerve to muscles of the neck.

items.name: Triangles of the neck
items.t: Its line separates the anterior and posterior triangles.

simpler.t: It works with the deep neck muscles to move the head, and its nerve is a cranial nerve.

facts.t: Skeletal muscle of the head develops from general mesoderm; trunk muscles come from somites.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Which embryonic tissue the sternocleidomastoid itself comes from.

facts.t: Its two heads, sternal and clavicular, can be seen and felt separately low in the neck.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). That the two heads are visible separately.

items.injury: A baby born with a shortened sternocleidomastoid on one side.
items.cannotDo: Hold the head straight: it tilts to the short side and turns away.
items.why: The short muscle pulls constantly, tilting to its own side and turning to the opposite.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Congenital torticollis.

items.injury: Injury to the accessory nerve in the neck.
items.damaged: The nerve to the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
items.cannotDo: Turn the head strongly to the opposite side, or shrug that shoulder.
items.why: Both muscles lose their motor supply from cranial nerve XI.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The accessory nerve’s supply to the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius, and the signs of its injury.

items.q: Explain why the left sternocleidomastoid turns the face to the right.
model: It runs from the front (sternum, clavicle) to the back of the skull (mastoid).
Pulling the mastoid down and forwards rotates the head.
The face turns to the opposite side.
So the left muscle turns the face to the right.

items.q: Compare the actions of the sternocleidomastoids and the semispinalis capitis acting on both sides.
model: Both sternocleidomastoids together flex the head.
Both semispinalis capitis muscles together extend it.
So the two pairs are antagonists.
Acting on one side, each pair turns and tilts the head.

items.q: Predict the head position in a baby whose right sternocleidomastoid is short.
model: The head tilts to the right.
The face turns to the left.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Congenital torticollis.

options: Mastoid process of the temporal bone
check.why: It inserts on the mastoid process of the temporal bone, named last in its name.

check.stem: What does one sternocleidomastoid do on its own?
options: Rotates the head to the opposite side
check.why: Individually it rotates the head to the opposite side.

check.stem: Which neck regions does it separate?
check.why: Seen from the side, it divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.
